window_margin_expt.notes: cp3 R2: m_expt, the experimental uncertainty budget of the all-experimental route for the registered reaction CaCO3 + 2 LiClO4 -> Ca(ClO4)2 + CO2 + 1/2 O2 + 2 Li (2 electrons). In that route Delta_G = DfH(Ca(ClO4)2) - 2 DfH(LiClO4) + DfG(CO2) - DfG(CaCO3), the LiClO4 free energies cancelling; the budget is the linear sum of the tabulated uncertainties of those inputs (as printed: 2 sigma for USGS B2131, the stated value for JANAF, the upper end of the NBS convention) plus the bound on the neglected exchange entropy times 298.15 K. A linear sum is used because the budget is a bound, not a standard deviation.

TA-005.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=DI water; phase=NMC811 aqueous dispersion (CMC/acrylic binder), no acid; surface=n.s.
TA-005.method: experiment: pH probe on filtrate of dilute dispersion
TA-005.notes: Li leaching drives dispersion pH in excess of 12 and corrodes the Al collector; H2 bubbles crack the dried coating. Phosphoric acid 0.5-1.5 wt% returns pH towards 4.5-8.5 window; with 1.0 wt% pH drifts above the threshold over 60 min, 1.5 wt% stays within it (Fig. 5, pdf p. 17).

TA-006.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NCM811 paste with Na-CMC 1.5 wt% + acrylate 1.5 wt%, 50% solids, after 1 h high-energy dispersion; surface=Al foil
TA-006.notes: Paste pH 11.44 without additive; authors state pH>9 dissolves the Al2O3 passivation layer, giving H2 evolution and pits >20 um in the dried electrode (pdf p. 4).

TA-007.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NCM811 paste with 5 wt% Li2SO4·H2O additive, Na-CMC/acrylate binder, 50% solids; surface=Al foil
TA-007.notes: Li2SO4 addition lowered pH only slightly (11.44 to 11.15 at 2 wt%, 11.05 at 5 wt%); still above the pH 9 threshold the authors cite.

TA-008.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water or water-isopropanol 80:20; phase=NMC811 slurry with 0.16 mmol H3PO4 per g NMC811, 50% solids, CMC/PAA/PEO/Na alginate binders; surface=Al or C-coated Al
TA-008.notes: pH modifier H3PO4 added before NMC; measured pH always below 9.0 just before coating. Exact values not printed.

TA-009.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NMC811 slurry, 2 wt% CMC + 1 wt% PMA, 0.16 g of 1 M H3PO4 per g NMC811, 60% solids; surface=22 um Al foil
TA-009.method: experiment: pH meter monitoring before coating
TA-009.notes: pH monitored to stay below 8.6 (the coating limit the authors cite); agglomeration reported above pH 10. Exact values not printed.

TA-010.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NMC811 slurry, CMC 1 wt% + latex 4 wt%, 69.3 wt% solids, no pH modifier; surface=corona-treated Al foil
TA-010.method: experiment: porous glass pH probe on centrifuged filtrate

TA-011.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NMC811 slurry, LiPAA 5 wt% (PAA neutralised with LiOH), 48.6 wt% solids, no pH modifier; surface=corona-treated Al foil
TA-011.method: experiment: porous glass pH probe on centrifuged filtrate
TA-011.notes: LiPAA coating showed no surface defects despite high slurry pH; authors suggest lower water content.

TA-012.conditions: T=22 C; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=NMC111/carbon black/kraft lignin (80:11:9) slurry, powder:water 1:1.7; surface=n.s.; time=1 day
TA-012.method: experiment: pH measurement during mixing (mean of two)
TA-012.notes: Lignin solution starts at pH 9.4 (alkali residues); slurry rises to 10.4 after first minute and stabilises at 10.5 after one day; diluting with twice the water did not change pH (Li leaching saturated).

TA-016.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 paste, 50 wt% solids, LiPAA binder with LiOH/PAA molar ratio above 0.6, 1 h stirring; surface=n.s.

TA-021.conditions: T=25 C; pH=12.5; I=derived; solvent=water; phase=washing solution of LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2, water:CAM 5:1, 1 h; surface=n.s.

TA-021.notes: Inputs as printed: cLiOH 29.0 mM, cLi2CO3 4.2 mM. Derivation: I = 1/2[(29.0+2*4.2)*1 + 29.0*1 + 4.2*4] = 29.0 + 3*4.2 = 41.6 mM, assuming full dissociation and carbonate as CO3^2-.

TE-061.conditions: T=0 K (electronic energies); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=gas phase; phase=molecular complexes; surface=n.a.; ligands=water, acetate, acetamide, N-methylmethanimine

TE-065.method: computation: B3-LYP, G96-LYP, CCSD(T), G3, W1C, W2C (Corral et al. 2003)

TE-066.notes: Monohydrate binding energy, Ca-O 2.213 A; protocol benchmark in SI Table S1 (not read). Literature cited: first-shell CN of Ca(H2O)n rises from 6 to 7-8 near n=12.

TE-067.method: computation: SMD continuum model, 6-31G* (Marenich, Cramer, Truhlar 2009)

TE-068.conditions: T=298 K; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water (implicit); phase=solutes; surface=n.a.; neutral solutes
TE-068.method: computation: SMD continuum model, 6-31G* (Marenich, Cramer, Truhlar 2009)

TE-069.conditions: T=0 K (electronic energies); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=gas phase; phase=molecular complexes; surface=n.a.; GMTKN55 main-group database

TE-071.method: computation: MOR41 benchmark vs DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS (Dohm et al. 2018)

TE-075.method: computation: GFN2-xTB vs DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS (Bannwarth, Ehlert, Grimme 2019)

TF-018.conditions: T=n.s. (ITC); pH=7; I=n.s. (no added salt stated); solvent=water; phase=aqueous PAA 5 mM monomer units with CaCl2 (AA:Ca 4:3); surface=n.a.

TF-018.notes: Derived: printed ln K = 10.1 (hetero-association model); log10 K = 10.1/2.3026 = 4.39. Symmetric two-site model gave ln K = 11.2 (log10 K 4.86). Fuhrer et al. 2020. Apparent constant per carboxylate of a polyelectrolyte, so it includes polyelectrolyte (condensation) effects; binding is endothermic and entropy driven per the authors.

TF-019.conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=0.1; solvent=water; phase=aqueous; surface=n.a.

TF-019.notes: Secondary citation (Martell & Smith 1974, Critical Stability Constants; also Hawley 1973). Monodentate carboxylate binding is weak; compare TD-051 (maleate, I = 0, 2.40).

Uncertainty scaled from +-0.2 mg/g. Argon atmosphere excludes CO2 uptake, so this is carbonate from the surface impurity only. Four times TA-019 (4.2 mM, NMC83), consistent with the higher Ni content and storage history.

TF-042.conditions: T=298.15 K; pH=n.a.; I=0; solvent=water; phase=aqueous; surface=n.a.
TF-042.notes: Source 53 = Plummer & Busenberg 1982. Numerically equal to pK2; DrH0 -3.167 kcal/mol.

TF-044.conditions: T=298.15 K; pH=n.a.; I=0; solvent=water; phase=aqueous; surface=n.a.

TF-049.conditions: T=25 C (ITS-90); pH=n.a.; I=0; solvent=water; phase=air-free liquid at 101.325 kPa; surface=n.a.

TF-049.notes: Air-saturated water at 25 C is 0.997041 g/cm3 (Table 1, p. 337). Original data: Kell 1975, J. Chem. Eng. Data 20, 97.

TF-050.conditions: T=298 K; pH=n.a.; I=0; solvent=water; phase=aqueous; surface=n.a.
TF-050.locator: pdf p. 1-2 (abstract) and pdf p. 6, Section 2
TF-050.method: compilation: cluster-pair value of Tissandier et al. 1998 adopted by Kelly et al. 2006
TF-050.notes: Author manuscript of Kelly, Cramer & Truhlar 2006; upgrades TD-059 from abstract. With a 1 atm gas standard state the Tissandier value is -264.0 kcal/mol (printed). Uncertainty: authors state no less than 2 kcal/mol.

TF-051.conditions: T=298 K; pH=n.a.; I=0; solvent=water; phase=aqueous; surface=n.a.; proton reference = -264.0 kcal/mol (Tissandier; 1 atm gas to 1 mol/L)
TF-051.locator: pdf p. 6, derived (rescaling of Marcus value)
TF-051.method: computation: rescaling of the Marcus 1991 value to the cluster-pair proton scale
TF-051.notes: Derived: Marcus value -359.7 kcal/mol on proton reference -1056 kJ/mol = -252.39 kcal/mol (both printed in 10.1021/ct400146w, TD-054); conventional shift dG(Ca) + 2[dG(H+,new) - dG(H+,Marcus)] = -359.7 + 2(-264.0 + 252.39) = -382.9 kcal/mol (-1602 kJ/mol).
